expansionSections.heading: Preparing For Your Blood Pressure Check
Pharmacy Screening Vs GP Blood Pressure Care

deepDiveBlocks.heading: Why High Blood Pressure Matters
paragraphs: Hypertension often causes no symptoms but increases the risk of stroke, heart disease and kidney problems over time — making routine screening valuable.
A pharmacy blood pressure check helps identify raised readings early and supports appropriate follow-up, whether that means lifestyle advice, repeat measurement or GP referral.

deepDiveBlocks.heading: Reading Your Results
paragraphs: Blood pressure is recorded as systolic (pressure when the heart beats) and diastolic (pressure when the heart rests) — measured in mmHg.

One raised reading does not diagnose hypertension. The NHS Hypertension Case-Finding Service may recommend ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) or GP follow-up depending on the result and your risk factors.

preparationGuide: Avoid caffeine 30 minutes before if possible
Wear loose sleeves for arm access
Bring previous home readings if you monitor
timelineNotes: Single check: baseline screening in pharmacy
Raised reading: repeat measurement or ABPM referral
Ongoing: regular checks for over-40s and high-risk groups
comparisonPoints: Pharmacy checks offer convenient screening without a routine GP appointment
Diagnosis and long-term treatment remain with your GP
Emergency symptoms such as chest pain require urgent care — not a pharmacy check alone
